sections.heading: What Cylinder Head Repair & Rebuild Involves

blocks.html: We strip, inspect, machine, and reassemble Jaguar cylinder heads to manufacturer tolerances. The process includes:

items: **Access & removal:** The cylinder head is removed from the engine bay — on many Jaguar engines this can be done with the engine in situ, though some models require engine removal for access.
**Full disassembly:** Valves, springs, camshafts, tappets, and cam-carriers are stripped. All components are cleaned in specialist solvent washers and kerosene baths.
**Pressure testing & crack detection:** The bare head is pressure-tested for leaks and checked for cracks using dye penetrant or Magnaflux equipment.

**Precision machining:** The deck surface is skimmed (resurfaced) to restore flatness. Valve seats are cut or replaced, and valve guides are pressed out and new ones installed using hydraulic presses.
**Valve reconditioning:** Valves are ground and re-seated. New valve stem seals are fitted.
**Reassembly & timing:** The head is reassembled with new gaskets and head bolts, then timed to the crankshaft using genuine timing tools.
**Final testing:** Before refitting, the head is re-pressure-tested to confirm integrity.

blocks.html: We use the same equipment and processes for all Jaguar engine families — from the classic AJ-V8 to the modern Ingenium range.

steps.title: Access & Removal
steps.body: We gain access to the cylinder head — often without engine removal. All ancillaries, manifolds, and timing components are carefully removed.

steps.title: Strip & Clean
steps.body: The head is fully disassembled; all valves, springs, tappets, and camshafts are removed. Components are cleaned in hot solvent washers.

steps.title: Pressure Test & Crack Check
steps.body: We pressure-test the bare head and use dye penetrant or Magnaflux to detect any cracks or porosity.

steps.title: Machining
steps.body: Skim the deck, cut new valve seats (multi-angle), and replace valve guides using hydraulic presses.

steps.title: Valve Work
steps.body: Grind valves, install new stem seals, and assemble the valve train with new springs and retainers.

steps.title: Reassembly & Timing
steps.body: Fit new head gaskets, torque new head bolts to specification, and set camshaft timing with genuine tools.

steps.title: Final Testing
steps.body: Pressure-test again, then refit the head to the engine and perform a full running test on our dyno.

items.q: Do you repair the cylinder head or replace it?
items.a: We always aim to repair and rebuild the original cylinder head, as it preserves the matching numbers and is often more cost-effective. Replacement is only recommended if the head is beyond economic repair (e.g., severe cracking).

items.q: What is included in a cylinder head rebuild?
items.a: A full rebuild includes: strip and clean, pressure testing, crack detection, skimming the deck, cutting or replacing valve seats, fitting new valve guides, grinding valves, fitting new stem seals, and reassembly with new gaskets and head bolts.

items.q: How long does cylinder head repair take?
items.a: Typically 3–5 working days from drop-off to completion, depending on parts availability and machining requirements. We'll give you a clear timeline when you book.

items.q: Do you need to remove the engine to do the cylinder head?
items.a: On many Jaguar engines, the head can be removed with the engine in the car. However, some models (e.g., XK, F-Type) may require engine removal for access. We assess this during inspection and quote accordingly.

items.q: What warranty do you offer on cylinder head work?
items.a: All our cylinder head repairs come with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty covering parts and labour. [Full warranty terms here →](/warranty)
